transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I keep losing these big chunks of time lately. I just... I find myself constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders on my computer that I just checked. And before I can even leave the house or start my workday, I end up mentally replaying conversations over and over. It's like I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with.
When you find yourself re-checking things or replaying conversations, do you feel a strong urge or anxiety that pushes you to do it, as if something bad will happen if you don't?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, it really comes down to feeling like I have to prove to myself that I didn't make some sort of serious mistake. 

If I don't go back and re-read those emails, or reopen the computer folders I just closed, I just... I can't settle down. The urge just keeps at me. I feel like I have to mentally replay the conversations or check the files again, otherwise I physically can't bring myself to leave the house or start my work. I just have to do it to be sure, and that's how I end up losing those big chunks of time every day.

When you feel this urge to re-check things, is it usually triggered by a specific intrusive thought or image that pops into your head about making a mistake, or is it more of a general worry about many different things in your life?

It's definitely more of a specific thought that just... barges in. It's not really a general worry about everything. 

Like, even when I'm sitting there trying to work through a system design for my job, this specific thought will suddenly hit me that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled some family photos, or maybe let someone in the community down. And I just can't seem to let it pass. Even though I know logically that I've already been over it and checked it, the thought just stays stuck in my head until I go back and look again.
When these thoughts about making a mistake pop into your head, do you recognize them as excessive or irrational, and do you try to resist or push them away before giving in to checking?

Yeah, I do know they're irrational. I mean, I'm a rational guy, I work in computers. But... I just can't seem to stop them. Like I mentioned, I'll be right in the middle of trying to work through a system design, or even preparing a lesson, and the thought just barges in anyway. It's always that same feeling that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I mishandled those family photos, or that I've let someone in the community down. 

I try to tell myself it's fine, that I've already checked, but I just can't seem to let it pass. I know I've been over it already, but I still end up giving in and checking again just to get the thought to stop.
How long have you been experiencing these intrusive thoughts and the urge to check or re-check things—weeks, months, or longer?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um, it's hard to pin down exactly when it started. 

It's definitely been longer than just a few weeks. I guess... maybe months, or even longer than that? I didn't really keep track of it at first, so I don't have an exact timeline for you. I just didn't really notice the exact point when it became such a big problem, it just sort of crept up on me over time.
On an average day, roughly how many hours would you say you spend re-checking, re-reading, or mentally replaying things because of these thoughts?

I haven't really timed it, to be honest. It's hard to put an exact number of hours on it because it's so scattered throughout the day. I might spend a few minutes here checking an email, then later I'll get stuck mentally going over a conversation for a while. It definitely adds up and takes a chunk out of my day, but I couldn't give you a specific number of hours.
Would you say these checking behaviors and intrusive thoughts significantly interfere with your work, relationships, or daily responsibilities, even if you can't pin down an exact number of hours?

Yeah, they definitely do. My work has slowed down enough that I've actually missed some design milestones recently. I've even had to postpone some mentoring sessions that I used to handle pretty reliably, just because I get so caught up in the checking. 

And it's not just my regular job, either. There's a youth coding workshop I help out with—something that really matters to me—and recently I was late and completely unprepared for it because I was stuck in one of those loops. I felt really embarrassed about letting them down. So, yes, it's definitely getting in the way.

Besides this checking and mental replaying, do you notice any other repetitive urges or rituals—like needing things arranged a certain way, excessive cleaning, or counting—that you feel compelled to do?

No, not really. I don't have any issues with cleaning or needing things lined up perfectly, and I don't find myself counting things either. It's really just the checking and the mental replaying that I get stuck on. That's the main thing.
